$schema-note: RR2-B003 narrow waiver matrix. Every entry is per-metric (an unlisted metric still must be 100%), time-boxed, owned, ticket-tracked and backed by substituteEvidence. Floors are the EXACT enforced floors, already adjusted for the documented child-process noise band of that module (Node built-in coverage varies ~+/-3 points between identical runs). The 6 files de-waived by RR2-B003 (cpuGuard.js, mmxCredentialBridge.js, deepRedactor.js, mmxResultRedactor.js, stateCorruptBackup.js, windowsNamePolicy.js) are deliberately ABSENT: the 100/100/100 rule governs them with no tolerance.
policy: No blanket tolerance. A waiver only lowers one metric of one file to one exact floor, scoped to the listed uncovered lines/branches. Expired or malformed waivers fail the gate.

assetPaths.js.reason: Line and function coverage are 100%. The three uncovered branches are lazy-cache guard arms in the assets-root resolution that only fire on first-call races; exercising them unit-wise would assert Node fs timing, not product logic.
assetPaths.js.substituteEvidence: Covered end-to-end by scripts/e2e real-release boot (every run resolves the assets root through these guards) and the installer acceptance suite.
assetPaths.js.remediation: Extract the cache-guard decision into a pure function and cover both arms in a dedicated unit test before expiry.

batches.js.reason: Uncovered lines are child-process spawn failure and cancellation-race arms (47, 55, 82-85, 144-146) that require killing live ffmpeg/mm processes mid-batch; unit-forcing them would assert scheduler timing instead of logic.
batches.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the e2e batch pipeline runs with the fake MMX and by the flakiness gate, which repeatedly exercises cancellation under concurrency.
batches.js.remediation: Introduce an injectable process-factory so spawn-failure and cancel-race arms become deterministic unit tests before expiry.

config.js.reason: Uncovered lines 180-190/202-205 are legacy config-migration arms that only trigger on pre-1.0 config files shipped with old installs; the pure parse/save paths are fully covered.
config.js.substituteEvidence: Migration arms are exercised by the real old->new upgrade acceptance scenario (RR2-H003) which installs a previous release into the same target directory.
config.js.remediation: Add fixture-driven unit tests with captured pre-1.0 config snapshots before expiry.

jobRegistry.js.reason: Uncovered lines 209-211 are the registry shutdown arm that fires only when the main process is killed mid-job; the one uncovered function is its private cleanup hook. All other metrics are 100%.
jobRegistry.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the deterministic interrupt/rollback acceptance scenario (RR2-H003 MINIMAX_INSTALL_FAULT_BEFORE_SWAP) and the endurance/resource suites which kill jobs mid-flight.
jobRegistry.js.remediation: Expose the shutdown hook through a test seam and cover it deterministically before expiry.

mmxApiKeySync.js.reason: Uncovered lines are live-MMX credential round-trip and process-kill arms (32-40, 69-70, 137-141) that require a real mmx binary and API credential; the redaction and validation logic is fully covered.
mmxApiKeySync.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the contract test suite with MMX_CONTRACT_OPTIONAL and the e2e-real pipeline run that performs a real credential sync against the mmx CLI.
mmxApiKeySync.js.remediation: Fake the mmx child process with a scripted responder so the sync round-trip becomes a deterministic unit test before expiry.

pathUtils.js.reason: Uncovered lines 32-33 are the Windows reserved-device rejection arm for inputs that Node's own fs layer refuses to create; the 65:* branches are the unreachable short-circuit halves of the isPathUnder null guards (normalize never returns a half-null pair for the tested inputs); every other path-traversal and normalization arm is fully covered. The scope was corrected on 2026-08-05 to list every BRDA key LCOV actually measures (10/10 gate snapshots stable), so the scope-honour safety net engages when Node's V8 percentage metric dips below the floor without any real coverage change.
pathUtils.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the security test suite (tests/security) and the path-grant contract tests which exercise hostile paths end-to-end.
pathUtils.js.remediation: Add the remaining reserved-device fixtures (NUL variants, trailing-space forms) as pure unit inputs before expiry.

providersPayloadSchema.js.reason: Uncovered lines 101-102/129-130 are defensive schema-violation arms that can only be reached by bypassing the IPC binding layer the RR2-C003 fix now enforces server-side.
providersPayloadSchema.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by providersKindBinding.rr2 tests plus the provider IPC contract suite which attacks every kind/id/origin combination through the real registrar.
providersPayloadSchema.js.remediation: Reach the defensive arms through a direct schema call in a unit test before expiry.

providersStore.js.reason: Uncovered regions are atomic-replace crash arms (135-161), concurrent-writer recovery (211-212, 247-252) and legacy-store migration from corrupt v0 formats (33, 44, 259-279) that require racing live file handles; the RR2-C003 kind-binding logic itself is 100% covered.
providersStore.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by providersKindBinding.rr2, the state-corruption recovery suite (stateCorruptBackup is 100/100/100) and the e2e provider round-trip runs.
providersStore.js.remediation: Introduce an injectable fs layer to deterministically simulate mid-write crashes and concurrent writers before expiry.

state.js.reason: Uncovered lines 23-24/453-455 are process-termination flush arms that only fire when the app is killed during a state write; the corruption-backup path (stateCorruptBackup.js) it delegates to is 100/100/100.
state.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the state-corruption recovery suite and the deterministic interrupt acceptance scenario (RR2-H003) which kills processes during writes.
state.js.remediation: Expose the flush hook through a test seam and cover the kill-during-write arms before expiry.

stateSanitizers.js.reason: All logic paths are covered except a single defensive default arm at line 211 that is unreachable through every sanctioned caller; the remaining uncovered branches are equivalent defensive defaults.
stateSanitizers.js.substituteEvidence: Covered by the deep-redaction suite (deepRedactor.js is 100/100/100) and the state round-trip contract tests which pass hostile payloads through the sanitizers.
stateSanitizers.js.remediation: Reach the defensive default via a direct type-violating call in a unit test before expiry.
